**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected plant part**: Stem/crown and root system — the image shows two plant stems photographed against a white background, with roots visible at the base.
- **Key features**:
  - Both stems show extensive **brown/tan internal vascular discoloration** running longitudinally through the tissue
  - The **outer stem surface** also shows brownish streaking/necrosis
  - The **root system is severely browned and necrotic** — fine roots are dead/collapsed
  - The **crown/basal area** shows extensive brown rot
  - No white mycelium visible (rules out Sclerotinia, Southern Blight)
  - No black sclerotia visible
  - No soft, water-soaked tissue (rules out Rhizopus Soft Rots)
  - No bacterial ooze apparent

**Reasoning:**

The hallmark sign here is the **internal brown vascular discoloration** running up through the stem, combined with root and crown necrosis. This is the classic presentation of a **vascular wilt** pathogen. Among the options:

- **Verticillium Wilt** causes exactly this: internal brown streaking in the vascular bundles, progressive from root upward, with root/crown decay — no surface mycelium or sclerotia
- Sclerotinia Timber Rot would show white cottony mycelium and black sclerotia inside the hollow stem
- Southern Blight would show white mycelium at soil line with tan sclerotia
- Bacterial Wilt diseases would typically show bacterial streaming/ooze

The longitudinal brown vascular streaking in both stems combined with fibrous root necrosis is most consistent with **Verticillium Wilt**.
